catalogue.title: Baseline
catalogue.description: The street as it is today.

catalogue.title: Cool roofs (albedo 0.25 → 0.70)
catalogue.description: High-albedo coating on every roof in view. Roofs have the highest sky view factor of any surface in the city and no neighbour shades them, so they take the full solar load.
catalogue.caveat: A roof is almost invisible to someone standing on the sidewalk, so this does very little for pedestrian comfort at street level. Its payoff is the top-floor cooling load and the citywide air temperature, neither of which a single-canyon model can resolve.

catalogue.title: Cool pavement (albedo 0.10 → 0.40)
catalogue.description: Reflective surface treatment on the roadbed. Cuts the heat stored in the asphalt and released after sunset.
catalogue.caveat: Reflected shortwave has to go somewhere, and in a canyon much of it goes into pedestrians and the facing walls. This scenario can lower the ground surface temperature while *raising* mean radiant temperature — a real and well-documented trade-off that a surface-temperature-only map would hide entirely.

catalogue.title: Street trees (40% canopy on the sunlit side)
catalogue.description: Continuous canopy along the sunlit sidewalk. Acts on three terms at once: intercepts the beam before it reaches the ground, moves absorbed energy into latent heat through transpiration, and replaces a hot surface in the pedestrian's view with a cool one.
catalogue.caveat: Canopy also reduces the sky view factor, which slightly slows night-time radiative cooling. Daytime gain dominates decisively, but the night penalty is real and the model reproduces it.

catalogue.title: External facade shading on the sunlit face
catalogue.description: Fixed external shading — brise-soleil, deep reveals, awnings — on the worst-exposed facade. Intercepts the beam outside the building envelope.
catalogue.caveat: Only affects the treated face, and does nothing for the sidewalk below unless it overhangs it.

catalogue.title: Everything at once
catalogue.description: Cool roofs, cool pavement, trees, and facade shading together.
catalogue.caveat: Effects are not additive: trees shade the pavement the cool coating was meant to fix, so the combined benefit is less than the sum of the parts. The model captures this because it re-solves rather than adding coefficients.

annual_note: Every monthly row is a full re-solve of that canyon at that month's representative-day peak hour, with that month's real solar geometry and meteorology. The annual columns are means over the twelve solved months, not a published coefficient applied twelve times. A positive seasonal_penalty means the intervention does less good in winter than in summer, which for a shading measure is the correct sign and is the cost of it.
